meta.landingTitle: ThirstCast: how thirsty the sky will be
meta.landingDescription: ThirstCast detects thirstwaves for Bengaluru Urban, Kolar and Mandya and estimates, in litres, the extra water crops and lakes lose.
meta.appDescription: Live thirstwave map, 7-day ET0 forecast, litres calculator and April 2024 replay for three Karnataka districts.
meta.methodsDescription: How ThirstCast detects thirstwaves, corrects forecast bias and converts excess ET0 into litres.

hero.pitch: Everyone forecasts how hot the air will be. Nobody forecasts how thirsty it will be. ThirstCast detects thirstwaves and tells you, in litres, what the sky is about to drink.
hero.sub: Detect unusual atmospheric water demand before it becomes a bigger challenge for farms and water managers. Seven-day thirstwave forecasts for three Karnataka pilot districts.
hero.pitchSub: ThirstCast uses ET₀ — reference evapotranspiration — and 30 years of local historical thresholds to detect multi-day thirstwaves and translate them into estimated extra water demand, in litres.
hero.art: Atmospheric globe showing Karnataka district markers

concept.title: From weather to water demand
concept.lead: ET₀ represents atmospheric evaporative demand: how strongly weather conditions drive water loss from a reference surface. When ET₀ stays above its local seasonal 90th percentile for three or more days, a thirstwave has begun.

cta.headline: See the water demand behind the weather.
cta.sub: Seven-day thirstwave forecasts. Litres per acre. Real historical data. Open API.

explainer.title: What is a thirstwave?
explainer.s1t: Heat, dry air, wind and sun
explainer.s1: Together they set how fast water can leave a crop or a lake.
explainer.s2: That pull is reference evapotranspiration, ET₀, in millimetres per day.
explainer.s3t: Three days above the local p90
explainer.s3: A thirstwave is 3 or more days in a row above the local day-of-year 90th percentile.
explainer.s4: Excess ET₀ is converted to extra irrigation need and surface-water evaporation loss.

evidence.title: Bengaluru Urban, April 2024
evidence.leadText: April 2024 was the highest-demand April for Bengaluru Urban since 1994 (ERA5, rank 1 of 31). The charts below use ERA5 reanalysis — not real-time data.
evidence.days: days with ET₀ above the day-of-year p90
evidence.litres: extra litres per acre, reference crop (estimate)
evidence.chart: April 2024 ET₀ versus the day-of-year p90, Bengaluru Urban
evidence.legend: Hatched bar: ET₀ above p90. Dashed line: day-of-year p90.
evidence.framing: Bengaluru's 2024 crisis was a supply failure. We don't claim thirstwaves caused it. We show the demand side nobody was measuring.
evidence.tmax: Maximum temperature was also above its own p90 on {n} of {total} days, so this is not a case of temperature staying quiet.
evidence.compare: The same April in the other pilot districts

why.title: Why it matters
why.body: Heat alerts say the air is hot. ThirstCast says how much faster water is leaving the surface, in litres, for a farmer, a lake manager and a city.
why.quote: This said, according to experts, there is essentially no data about extreme thirstwaves over India.
why.paper: Weighted for cropland area harvested, thirstwave intensity, duration, and frequency have increased by 0.06 mm d⁻¹ decade⁻¹, 0.10 days decade⁻¹, and 0.39 events decade⁻¹, respectively during 1981–2021. Statistically significant trends appear across 17%, 7%, and 23% of cropland area for intensity, frequency, and duration.

features.title: Platform capabilities
features.f1: Three districts, coloured by ACTIVE, WATCH or NONE, with a pattern as well as a colour.
features.f2: Bias-adjusted ET₀ beside the local day-of-year p90.
features.f3: Extra irrigation per acre, as a range, for the crops configured in that district.
features.f4: Extra evaporation for verified lake and reservoir areas. An upper bound.
features.f5: Ask the agent in either language. Answers carry a mode badge and a caveat.
features.f6: Districts, thirstwave, replay and ask. No login.
features.f7: The product can mail a new ACTIVE status. Signup in this preview does not collect an address.

pilots.title: Pilot districts
pilots.lead: Each district represents a different water-stress context: urban lakes, dryland agriculture, and reservoir-irrigated crops.

try.title: Try a question
try.body: These open the dashboard with the AI chat pre-filled. Nothing is sent until you press Ask.

api.title: Open data and API
api.body: The same JSON the map reads. Replace $API with the deployed ApiUrl, without a trailing slash.

limits.title: Honest limits
limits.l1: District-centroid estimate (~10 km grid). Not a field, and not the lake surface itself.
limits.l2: Every litre is an estimate with a range. Lake figures are upper bounds.
limits.l3: This is a research prototype. ET₀ is standard. Event-based thirstwave detection, locally thresholded and translated into litres per stakeholder, exists today as a research prototype in the US. To our knowledge, we are first to build it for India.
limits.l4: Forecast skill falls after a few days. The bias correction is a mean offset only.

app.acresError: Enter a number from 0.1 to 10,000, in steps of 0.1.

app.mockNote: MOCK: historical ERA5 data for {date} evaluated as if it were a forecast (no bias correction). Not live.
app.formula: Shown range = the forecast endpoint's per-acre range × acres. That range is excess millimetres × Kc × 4,047 L, with Kc ±10%. Kc for {crop} is {kc} (FAO-56, mid-season).
app.excessDef: Sum of daily ET₀ above the local day-of-year p90 threshold
app.summaryActive: A thirstwave is underway at the district centroid.
app.summaryWatch: No 3-day run today, but at least one day in the 7-day window is above the ET₀ p90.
app.summaryNone: No day in the 7-day window is above the ET₀ p90.
app.summaryUnknown: The detector has not published a status yet.
app.waveExtends: It may continue past the forecast.
app.heatIntro: ET₀ and maximum temperature do not have to cross their own p90 thresholds on the same days.
app.heatCount: In this 7-day window: ET₀ above p90 on {et}, Tmax above its p90 on {tx}, both on {both}.
app.blindTitle: A hot-season example where temperature stayed at or below its own p90

app.blindCount: The blindspot file records {n} such thirstwaves across the three districts (Bengaluru Urban {b}, Kolar {k}, Mandya {m}).
